comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Brainstorm decision and OSS prior-art audit (2026-09-02)

User decision: rebar must not execute Terraform itself, and should reuse authoritative, actively maintained OSS projects for Terraform validation/analysis wherever possible rather than reimplementing their logic. Treat orchestration, isolation, provenance, normalization, and policy as rebar-owned; treat Terraform parsing/rules as upstream-owned.

Current prior-art findings:
- TFLint (terraform-linters/tflint, 5.8k stars, active 2026-08-29) is the closest analog. It does not invoke Terraform. It statically parses/evaluates HCL using HCL/cty plus a fork of Terraform internals, treats dynamic values as unknown, and emits JSON/SARIF. Its bundled Terraform-language rules need no downloaded plugin. It does launch ruleset subprocesses, so rebar must supply its own config and allow only the bundled ruleset; never honor repository plugin config or run tflint --init. Remote modules are not fetched by default and require prior terraform init/get plus opt-in --call-module-type=all; rebar should use --call-module-type=none or a deliberate local-only policy.
- HashiCorp terraform-config-inspect is a narrow, authoritative source parser/CLI. It explicitly processes only stable top-level module metadata to reduce synchronization burden. Good for extracting provider/module declarations, variables, outputs, and resources; not a semantic validator.
- Checkov (9k stars, active 2026-08-30) statically parses Terraform and builds a graph without invoking Terraform. External-module downloads are disabled unless requested; --framework terraform --download-external-modules false --skip-download provides a plausible offline, structured-output adapter. Its authority is security/misconfiguration policy, not Terraform acceptance.
- Trivy (37.7k stars, active 2026-09-01) corroborates the static-analysis pattern and explicitly treats data sources/computed values as unknown. However its Terraform parser allows remote-module downloads by default, and its CLI flag only excludes downloaded-module findings rather than clearly disabling downloads. It is not the safest first adapter without an egress sandbox.
- terraform-docs is not a safe generic adapter merely because it normally parses source: project/config options can cause it to run terraform output -json, and it supports executable plugins.
- terraform-ls is not static-only. It automatically invokes terraform version -json and terraform providers schema -json for recognized roots; formatting, validation, init, and other paths invoke more Terraform operations. It also makes Registry/Algolia requests. It can only be made non-executing through a pinned-version, scrubbed-environment containment contract, so it should not be the v1 authority.
- Across mature tools, static analysis is explicitly incomplete: unknown runtime/cloud values remain unknown; source findings are advisory; higher-fidelity plan analysis consumes an already-produced plan/plan JSON rather than creating one.

Design implication: replace REB-640's current terraform validate/live-terraform plan execution premise. The likely lane is (1) source/module metadata from an authoritative parser, (2) curated static diagnostics from TFLint and optionally a security scanner, and (3) optional analysis of a caller/CI-supplied plan artifact. Rebar never initializes modules/providers, executes Terraform/OpenTofu/provider binaries, or acquires cloud credentials.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
New OSS safety/correctness finding (2026-09-03; design decision pending)

The previously selected tfparse backend is not safe to treat as a confined evaluator merely by setting allow_downloads=False. In current tfparse 0.6.21 source:
- converter.handleFunctionCall builds Trivy/defsec's Terraform function map and evaluates functions.
- relativeResolveFs.Open is explicitly documented as allowing relative paths outside the filesystem root and calls os.Open on the joined path.
- The upstream test corpus intentionally evaluates file(), fileexists(), and fileset(), including ../ traversal and absolute paths.
- Fallback function evaluation substitutes cty.EmptyObjectVal for a variable with no default, then may invoke the function; therefore a returned concrete value is not necessarily proof that the real Terraform value is concrete.

Consequences: a subprocess protects Rebar from native crashes but does not confine reads; allow_downloads=False only addresses module fetching. Whole-module parsing also does not make fallback values semantically authoritative. Unless a portable filesystem sandbox or an upstream no-I/O/no-fallback-evaluation mode exists, v1 should not invoke tfparse on arbitrary client Terraform. Candidate replacement is side-effect-free structural parsing plus authoritative PATH corroborators, with computed attribute values returning abstain.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Confirmed design decision (2026-09-03)\n\nV1 will not use tfparse evaluation. The guaranteed backend is side-effect-free structural analysis of the complete affected module/local impact closure: declarations, references, module/provider sources, source spans, and literal values only. Any computed attribute value returns abstain. Authoritative locally available tools such as terraform-config-inspect, TFLint, or Trivy may corroborate a narrowly matching query under Rebar-owned safe configuration; they do not originate findings, and a clean/absent diagnostic never proves correctness. Semantic evaluation is deferred until an upstream no-I/O mode or a portable strong sandbox exists.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Additional corroborator safety correction (2026-09-03)

TFLint must also be excluded from v1 execution without a strong filesystem sandbox. Current TFLint embeds Terraform's filesystem functions (file, fileexists, fileset, filebase64, file hashes, templatefile); its openFile canonicalizes absolute/relative/~ paths but does not confine them to the module/repository. Rebar-owned config, bundled-rules-only, and --call-module-type=none prevent repository plugin/module execution and fetching, but they do not prevent Terraform source from causing arbitrary readable host files to be opened during evaluation.

HashiCorp terraform-config-inspect remains a viable optional PATH corroborator: its shallow loader uses HCL Expr.Value(nil), exposes only stable top-level module metadata, and does not register Terraform functions. V1 should use it only on a hardened repo snapshot, schema-check its JSON, capture its binary digest/version provenance, and abstain on errors/skew. Trivy remains deferred unless an invocation is proven both no-egress and filesystem-confined.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Brainstorm complete and approved (2026-09-03).

The design is decomposed into four dependency-ordered executable tasks:
1. `forcible-diminished-lamb` — plan-review Terraform structural grounding vertical slice.
2. `salmon-abominable-pupa` — code-review IaC grounding; depends on S1.
3. `depraved-classless-rooster` — local/registry source probing; depends on S2.
4. `schematic-gleesome-ballpython` — optional `terraform-config-inspect` corroboration; depends on S3.

The leaves are typed `task` (correcting the earlier childless-`story` authoring mismatch). `next_batch(yaw-quota-wraith)` now returns S1 alone. S1 has a current signed plan-review PASS (job `1788478341336192000-84aea946da9343fba8b3508cb2d89626`, verified at `ebbcd7a030d6029216127c83fb43c415117af366`). The blocked descendants were intentionally not reviewed; review each only after its predecessor closes.

Approved boundary:
- Terraform support is isolated behind the `grounding-terraform` extra with exact direct dependency `python-hcl2==8.1.3`; core and non-Terraform projects gain no Terraform-specific dependency or tools.
- The feature grounds LLM-generated IaC findings for Terraform-routed Pass 1 and gives Pass 2 a fresh, independent re-grounding session. It does not duplicate mechanical Terraform validation suited to CI.
- Whole affected-module indexing includes sibling files, literal in-repo child modules, and in-repo reverse callers so file-scoped evidence cannot silently misstate module-wide symbols.
- Rebar never executes Terraform, OpenTofu, providers, repository plugins/config, TFLint, Trivy, tfparse, terraform-ls, or terraform-docs. The only optional executable is `terraform-config-inspect`, run under the separately specified copied-snapshot, hardened subprocess contract.
- V1 reads local content already available in the client project and treats remote sources as metadata only. Remote content fetch using ambient credentials is approved as a documented future extension if demand justifies it. Every access failure abstains; 401/403/404 never prove nonexistence.
- Limits are 64 modules, 5,000 files, 32 MiB, and 60 seconds. A limit or safety failure returns one abstention and no partial facts.

Parser evidence correction: an isolated exact-wheel probe showed that serialized `SerializationOptions(with_meta=True)` does not provide the planned source ranges. The implementation contract now uses public `hcl2.parses_to_tree(text)` and Lark `Tree.meta`, with `propagate_positions=True` confirmed upstream. Serialized metadata is explicitly not an oracle.

No production code was changed or claimed during brainstorming.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Rebar's plan-review T10 and code-review IaC agents can inspect Terraform as text, but generic file search does not reliably answer module-wide questions: Terraform loads every `.tf` and `.tf.json` file in a module together, local modules cross directory boundaries, and computed values are unknowable without runtime context. That makes unsupported LLM claims about declarations, references, and sources a false-positive/false-negative risk.

This feature supplies query-scoped evidence for LLM findings. It does not duplicate mechanical Terraform validation that belongs in project CI, and it never executes Terraform, OpenTofu, a provider binary, or an apply/plan/validate operation.

## Outcome

Ship an optional `grounding-terraform` extra containing `python-hcl2==8.1.3`. When installed, Terraform tools are exposed only to Terraform-routed Pass-1 and Pass-2 agents in plan review and code review. Core Rebar and projects without Terraform retain the same dependency closure and tool surface.

The final tool surface is:

- `lookup_declaration`: locate a statically addressable declaration and its source location.
- `resolve_reference`: resolve conservative module-scope traversals, including local child outputs, without evaluating expressions or provider schemas.
- `probe_source`: inspect repo-contained local sources and positive registry metadata reachable with existing ambient credentials; it never downloads module contents.
- `corroborate_diagnostic`: independently match a narrow structural diagnostic using an audited `terraform-config-inspect` binary already on `PATH`.

Every call returns the existing `refuted | match | abstain` evidence shape plus a canonical receipt containing the normalized query, code/module digest, backend/version/config, outcome, and result digest. Tool output contains source paths, spans, structural classifications, and hashes, but never credentials or raw literal values.

## Scope and mechanics

- Scope starts from changed or declared `.tf` / `.tf.json` paths. Each affected directory is indexed as one whole Terraform module. The bounded closure follows literal, repo-contained local module sources forward and discovers in-repo literal reverse callers. A changed `.tfvars` file is inspectable directly but is never treated as selected input: Rebar cannot know which variable file Terraform would load.
- A per-agent-call session owns an immutable parse cache and query ledger. Pass 2 must issue its own tool query; it may reuse immutable parse data but cannot accept a Pass-1 receipt as verification.
- The parser receives already-read file bytes in the existing 60-second grounding worker boundary. Out-of-repo paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. Syntax errors, duplicate/ambiguous declarations, computed values, provider-defined attributes, dynamic sources, and runtime-dependent expressions abstain.
- The whole query abstains without partial conclusions if its closure exceeds 64 modules, 5,000 Terraform files, or 32 MiB.
- Actual repository reads are merged into agent usage as synthetic file reads. Membership globs for `**/*.tf` and `**/*.tf.json` use the existing signed read-set glob hashing so a later sibling file addition invalidates plan-review evidence without requiring the optional parser at claim time.
- Registry access is positive-only. Environment `TF_TOKEN_<hostname>` credentials and static Terraform credential files may be used with Terraform's precedence rules. Rebar never prompts, executes credential helpers, returns tokens, or treats 401/403/404, TLS/proxy failures, timeouts, rate limits, or malformed responses as proof that a source does not exist.
- V1 does not fetch remote module contents. The ADR records that remote fetch using ambient credentials is approved as a future extension if demand justifies it, with the same containment, redaction, and abstention rules.
- `terraform-config-inspect` is the only optional executable allowed in V1. It receives a minimal copied snapshot of approved module files, closed stdin, a scrubbed environment, and a bounded process group; its JSON is schema-checked and its absolute path, binary digest, and discoverable version are recorded. Absence, output skew, errors, or a non-match abstain. TFLint, Trivy, tfparse, terraform-ls, terraform-docs, Terraform, OpenTofu, and provider executables are not invoked.

## Positive rationale

Conservative structural evidence addresses the LLM's uncertainty while keeping deterministic validation in client CI. `python-hcl2` owns HCL parsing, HashiCorp's shallow `terraform-config-inspect` provides optional independent corroboration, and Rebar owns only safe orchestration, scope closure, redaction, receipts, and review routing. Abstention is preferable to recreating Terraform evaluation semantics.

## Out of scope

- Running `terraform validate`, `terraform plan`, `terraform init/get`, OpenTofu, providers, policy scanners, plugins, or repository-supplied executable/config hooks.
- Evaluating expressions, cloud state, provider schemas, variable precedence, or whether an arbitrary `.tfvars` file is selected.
- Accepting a caller-produced plan artifact; the subject is Terraform in the client project running Rebar.
- Downloading or executing remote module content in V1.
- Turning grounding into a scanner or a standalone CI validator. Tools answer agent queries and do not originate findings.

## Decomposition

1. A plan-review vertical slice ships the optional parser/index, `lookup_declaration`, `resolve_reference`, signed read receipts, and Terraform-only Pass-1/Pass-2 routing.
2. A dependent code-review slice reuses that session for the IaC overlay and its verifier.
3. A dependent source-probe slice adds local and positive registry-source evidence with ambient-credential redaction and access-error abstention.
4. A dependent authoritative-corroboration slice adds the sole allowlisted `terraform-config-inspect` adapter and live contract canary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Installing `nava-rebar[grounding-terraform]` adds exactly `python-hcl2==8.1.3`; lean-core subprocess tests prove `import rebar` and non-Terraform reviews neither import `hcl2` nor advertise Terraform tools.
- [ ] Plan-review T10 Pass 1 and evidence-bearing Pass 2 can independently call `lookup_declaration` and `resolve_reference` over the complete bounded affected-module closure; non-Terraform criteria cannot see those tools.
- [ ] Code-review IaC Pass 1 and evidence-bearing Pass 2 receive the same grounding operations for changed Terraform, while non-IaC overlays and reviews do not.
- [ ] `probe_source` returns positive local/registry evidence only from repo-contained files or metadata reachable with ambient credentials, and every access/error/ambiguity arm returns a closed abstention without asserting nonexistence.
- [ ] `corroborate_diagnostic` can report only a matching, schema-valid `terraform-config-inspect` result from the hardened snapshot; a clean/absent/skewed/error result abstains and no other Terraform-related executable is launched.
- [ ] Canonical receipts redact credentials and literal payloads, and signed plan-review read sets include every concrete Terraform file read plus membership protection that detects a newly added module sibling.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0111-terraform-structural-grounding.md` records the trust boundary, OSS rationale, V1 prohibitions, and approved future ambient-credential remote-fetch direction; `docs/grounding.md` documents install, routing, limits, outcomes, and abstentions.

## Verification

Each child carries tier-specific commands and observable oracles. The epic is verified by the union of those child criteria; no live Terraform/cloud execution is part of completion.
